meta.title: Check your understanding: The p-n junction

objectives: Describe how doping with phosphorus and boron makes n-type and p-type silicon
Explain how the built-in field at a p-n junction turns electron–hole pairs into a current
Calculate the built-in potential and predict how it changes with doping

questions.prompt: A photon makes an electron–hole pair in the p-type base of a cell. What job does the junction's built-in field do?
choices: It creates the electron–hole pairs that light alone cannot
It pulls electrons and holes together so their energy is released
It sweeps electrons to the n side and holes to the p side, keeping them apart
It raises the band gap so fewer photons are wasted as heat
questions.explain: Light makes the pairs; the field sorts them. An electron that reaches the depletion region is swept to the n side and holes go to the p side, so they flow out through a circuit instead of recombining. Pulling them together would be recombination, which is exactly what the field prevents.

questions.prompt: The lesson's junction has N_A = 10¹⁶ cm⁻³ and N_D = 10¹⁹ cm⁻³, giving a built-in potential of about 0.895 V. If the p-type base is doped ten times more heavily (N_A = 10¹⁷ cm⁻³), what does V_bi become?
questions.explain: V_bi grows with the logarithm of the doping, so ten times more on one side adds kT/q × ln 10 ≈ 60 mV: 0.895 + 0.060 ≈ 0.95 V. It does not grow tenfold, and more doping makes the step taller, not shorter.

questions.prompt: With the load set to a short circuit, the cell in the explorer delivers its largest current. How much power does it deliver?
choices: Its maximum power, since the current is at its highest
About half of its maximum power
More than at the maximum power point, because no voltage is wasted
None, because the voltage across it is zero
questions.explain: Power is current times voltage. At short circuit the current is highest but the voltage is zero; at open circuit the voltage is highest but the current is zero. Both ends give no power, and the most power comes from a load in between, at the maximum power point.

questions.prompt: In the lesson's junction the boron-doped p side has a thousand times fewer dopant atoms per cm³ than the phosphorus-doped n side. Where does most of the depletion region lie?
choices: On the heavily doped n side, where there are more ions
On the lightly doped p side, which must uncover a thicker layer of ions
Split equally, because the two sides carry equal charge
In the metal contacts at the two ends of the cell
questions.explain: The uncovered charge must be equal on both sides. A lightly doped side has few ions per cm³, so it has to uncover a much thicker layer to match: almost all of the 0.34 µm lies on the p side. Equal charge does not mean equal width.
